source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #352 (branch fix/334-borrowed-drop at head f6259d5774847b67d16a76c0375a29c40d27a12e — the #334 change (an owned resource cannot be dropped or have its ownership transferred while a borrow of it is lent to a call in flight: handle-table entries carry a borrow count, borrows lent across a call boundary are registered against the destination table by resource-record identity for the call's duration, and the transfer walk resolves every borrowed identity before moving any owned argument) with the Codex-review follow-ups, merged with current main 98e93a3d10354bee4a4a27e9b77252d69f066777 (PR #349, the #335 handle validation); ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45620056819 and 45620073895 against the branch and pull-request run 45620003493, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #352 (#334, dropping an owned resource while it is borrowed traps; fourth re-baseline for this PR, for the final integration with PR #349 (#335), which changed the same handle machinery over three Codex-review rounds: canonical handle operations validate handle indices against the instance table, host-supplied public-call arguments are registered at the call boundary, a resource.drop naming a host handle wins over a colliding local entry, and a borrow of a locally defined resource crosses the boundary as its representation rather than a handle index. The merge keeps both invariants at once: the caller's borrow arguments are validated before the transfer walk rewrites their indices, lifted result handles are validated after lifting, and the drop path validates the handle before the borrowed check). Attribution was isolated by measuring current main alone three times (workflow_dispatch runs 45618952163, 45618969889 and 45618983894 on main at 98e93a3d10354bee4a4a27e9b77252d69f066777; all three runs pass the gate against main's checked-in baseline, and the main control is byte-identical to that baseline on all 32 gated series). This PR's own delta against the main control is confined to the series of the three configurations that link telomere-component: in release, stripped file +10,688 B (component, wasi) / +10,672 B (wasi-threads) and stripped .text +9,456 B in each; in release-size, stripped file +6,896 B in each and stripped .text +5,616 B (component, wasi) / +5,632 B (wasi-threads). Every other configuration is byte-identical to main in both profiles. Against the previous (third) re-baseline of this PR, measured before PR #349 landed, the step is +8,704 B stripped file in release for each of the three configurations and +7,072 B (component) / +7,088 B (wasi, wasi-threads) stripped .text; in release-size, +5,720 B stripped file in each and +4,368 B (component, wasi-threads) / +4,352 B (wasi) stripped .text — the #335 change now present in the tree accounts for the step — and all twelve series are re-baselined to the branch measurements; every other baseline is unchanged. Run-to-run spread was 0 B for every gated series across the three branch samples and across the three main samples. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth is the release component stripped file series at +11.86% (2,433,656 B to 2,722,336 B). The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison.
